blocks.text: Managing training content on macOS

Training coordinators often juggle multiple files and learning modules. Using PowerPoint on Mac requires a solid grasp of the interface. Microsoft 365 for Mac is the standard for these tasks. Ensure you have 8 GB of RAM for the smoothest experience. If your app hangs, check for conflicting add-ins first. You can often clear these by restarting the application.
Essential shortcuts for faster work

Mac users have unique keyboard shortcuts that differ from Windows. Memorize these to stop clicking through menus. Use ⌘ + Shift + N to insert a new slide instantly. Grouping your elements is vital for complex training graphics. Select your items and press ⌘ + Option + G to group them. This keeps your layout clean when moving items around the slide.
Working with the Slide Master

The Slide Master is your best friend for long training decks. Go to View > Slide Master to change layouts globally. This prevents you from editing every single slide one by one. It saves hours of manual work. Use this for adding company logos or standard footers. If you need help finding the Master view, ask Lazur to point it out.
Common technical hurdles

Syncing errors are common when using OneDrive. If your files go missing, check your internet connection. Make sure you are signed into the correct Microsoft account. Many users struggle with authentication errors. Verify your subscription status in the File menu if features appear locked. Do not rely on local saves if you need real-time collaboration.

items: Use high-resolution images but compress them to keep file size low.
Avoid too many animations that can slow down older Mac models.
Keep text minimal to ensure your learners focus on your voice.
Use consistent fonts across all your training materials.
Save your final presentation as a PDF if you only need a handout.

blocks.text: Organizing your training library

You likely have hundreds of slides across different courses. Keep your file naming convention consistent. Use dates and version numbers in every filename. This makes searching in Finder much faster. If you need to find a specific slide quickly, use the search bar in the thumbnails pane. You can also use the Outline view to edit text without opening each slide.
If you are stuck on a specific formatting task, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the tool is. Lazur will draw a circle around the exact menu item for you.

blocks.text: Improving slide accessibility

Training materials must be accessible to all employees. Always add alt text to your images. Right-click your image and select Edit Alt Text. This helps screen readers describe your content. Keep your contrast high between text and backgrounds. Use the built-in accessibility checker in the Review tab to find issues.
Advanced layout techniques

Alignment is key for professional training decks. Use the Arrange menu to distribute objects evenly. You can snap objects to the grid to keep them perfectly aligned. If you are struggling with precise placement, zoom in on your slide. Press ⌘ + plus sign to zoom in. Use the guides to mark your margins.
Handling large media files

Videos can make your PowerPoint file massive. This often leads to performance issues during presentations. Compress your media files before inserting them into your slides. Use a tool like Handbrake to convert videos to a smaller format. If you have too many videos, consider linking to them online instead. This keeps your presentation file light and fast.
What to do when PowerPoint freezes

PowerPoint might stop responding if you have too many complex objects. Force quit the app by pressing ⌘ + Option + Esc. Select Microsoft PowerPoint and click Force Quit. Reopen the app and check the AutoRecover pane. Most of your work should be saved if you had AutoSave enabled. Always enable AutoSave to your OneDrive account.
Automating your workflow

You do not need to do everything manually. Use templates for your recurring training decks. Create a standard deck with your branding and save it as a template. You can then start new presentations from this file. This ensures every training session looks professional and consistent. It also saves you from recreating the same layout every week.
Final presentation tips

Before you start your training session, test your setup. Connect your Mac to the projector or screen early. Check your presenter view settings in the Slide Show tab. Make sure your speaker notes are visible only to you. If you need to hide your cursor, use the settings in the slide show menu. A clean presentation keeps your audience focused on the content.

faq.question: Can I use PowerPoint on Mac for free?
faq.answer: PowerPoint is part of Microsoft 365. You need a subscription to use all features, though a free web version is available for basic editing.

faq.question: Why is my PowerPoint so slow on Mac?
faq.answer: Slow performance is often caused by large file sizes or too many high-resolution images. Try compressing your media and closing other demanding apps.

faq.question: How do I add a new slide on Mac?
faq.answer: The fastest way to add a new slide is pressing ⌘ + Shift + N on your keyboard.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside PowerPoint?
faq.answer: Lazur works on top of any app on your Mac. You can ask it to guide you to tools or explain how to use specific PowerPoint features.
